The pressure differences are real (rho x g x h = 1,030 x 10 x 0.10 = 1,030 Pa; 1,000 Pa; 920 Pa, recomputed) and a water U-tube would show 1,030/10,000 = 10.3 cm, 10.0 cm and 9.2 cm. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL Learners first observe that the three streams land at about the same distance (the speed of a jet depends on depth, not on density), so jets cannot show the effect of density. A simple pressure gauge (a funnel covered with thin balloon rubber, joined by a clear tube to a U-tube of coloured water) is then lowered to 10 cm in each liquid, by the teacher or one group at a time. The water in the U-tube stands highest for salt water (about 10.3 cm), lower for water (10.0 cm) and lowest for oil (9.2 cm); learners measure the differences with a ruler. phys_3_3 G4.issue: Warming a diode cannot show the semiconductor temperature trend with a bulb (change about 2 percent); the lesson now says so and offers a thermistor and multimeter if available, plus real temperature data Warming a forward-biased diode by about 25 K lowers its forward voltage by only about 2 mV per K, about 50 mV out of 3 V (about 2 percent change in a bulb current near 0.15 A), so no bulb change can be seen, and the diode is a doped p-n device, not pure silicon. So the lesson's 'small change' was not a realistic observation and did not test the trend. KICD outcome c asks learners to investigate behaviour with varying temperatures, so a thermistor (a semiconducting material whose resistance falls with temperature; a typical 10 kilo-ohm one goes from about 10 to about 5 kilo-ohm between 25 C and 40 C, checked as 10 x exp(3950 x (1/313 - 1/298)) = about 5.3) is offered as a measurable option. Teacher decides whether such parts are available locally. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL Then she warms the diode in a sealed bag in hand-hot water while students watch the bulb; they will probably see little or no change and should record exactly that (a diode is a doped device, not a pure-silicon sample, and a torch bulb cannot show a change this small). If a digital multimeter and an NTC thermistor (for example from an old electronic thermometer or charger) are available, use them for the same warming step: on the resistance range the reading falls clearly as the thermistor warms, which shows the semiconductor trend directly.
